m: Attractively lively and animated.
Making indirect reference to something.
Having the ability to assess situations accurately; shrewd.
t: Cousin of « astucieux »: an astute investor.

m: To begin.
Recovering from illness.
To restrain or keep in check.
t: Same family as « courber »: a curb on a horse is a strap. Curb inflation.

m: To bring a feeling or memory to mind.
To be constantly or visibly anxious.
t: Worry eats at you. Don't fret = ne t'en fais pas.

m: Wilful and obstinate.
Anger.
To calm or send to sleep; (n.) a pause.
t: Lullaby: lull a baby; a lull in the storm = « accalmie ».

m: To render ineffective by countering.
Attempting to impress by affecting greater importance than is possessed.
Very great or intense; having great depth.
A source of help in a difficult situation; resort.
t: Same as « recours »: avoir recours à. Without recourse = sans recours.

m: To return to a former, less developed state.
An unintended consequence.
t: Same as « répercussion ». Usually plural: repercussions.

m: To fill up again.
t: Re + plein: fill again. Cousin of « plénitude ».

m: Keeping careful watch for danger.
Well meaning and kindly.
To scold or criticize angrily.
t: Be-rate: dressing someone down. Not related to « rate » (tax).

m: Able to float; cheerful and optimistic.
t: Une bouée floats: buoyant mood. Also a buoyant market is rising.

m: To accept or allow behaviour that is wrong.
f: cautionner, excuser, fermer les yeux sur
t: Donner: you give it a pass. Not 'approve': condone = tolerate wrong.

m: To violate a law or rule.
t: Same as « contrevenir »: contravene a law.

m: To publicly declare to be wrong or evil.
Exercising absolute power in a cruel way.
To depart from an established course.
t: Same as « dévier »: off the road.

m: To increase rapidly; to become more intense.
t: Escalier: step up. A conflict escalates = « s'envenime ».

m: To drive out an evil spirit; to get rid of a painful memory.
Fussy about details; hard to please.
t: Finicky about food: « difficile »; about details: « tatillon ».

m: To prevent from succeeding.
t: Foil a plot = déjouer un complot. (Also n.: a contrasting character.)

m: Twisted together; closely connected.
Impossible to break or change.
t: Clad in iron: an ironclad contract is airtight. « Blindé ».

m: To put at risk of harm or failure.
e: Old French jeu parti (divided game, even chances).
t: « Jeu parti »: a gamble with even odds. Jeopardy = péril.

m: Not aware of or concerned about what is happening around.
To carry out a harmful or illegal act.
t: Same as « perpétrer ». The perpetrator = auteur du crime.

m: Sounding sad and mournful.
To say again for emphasis.
To overcome (a difficulty); to be on top of.
Very skilled; proficient.
t: « Adepte » = follower. English: an adept = someone skilled at something.

m: Harmful or unfavourable.
t: Not « adverse » (opponent). Adverse effects, adverse weather = conditions défavorables. Not 'averse'.

m: A very typical example; an original model.
Decisive; ending all doubt.
To make secret plans jointly for an unlawful act.
To free from entanglement; to untangle.
Weakness; vulnerability.
A real or imagined cause for complaint.
t: « Grief » (also in French legal speak): a heavy burden. Cousin of « grave ».

m: Graceful, self-assured balance in manner.
Self-importance; ostentatious speech.
The authority to represent someone else; a stand-in.
e: Contraction of procuracy, Latin procurare (to take care of).
t: Proxy = « procuration ». Use as a proxy for.

m: To yield after initially refusing.
t: Cousin of « ralentir ». Soften your stance: « céder ».

m: The quality of being extremely thorough and strict.
Thinly dispersed or scattered.
Open to doubt; possibly dishonest.
Too long, slow or dull.
The state of being strong and active.
To produce; to give way.
t: Rendement (n.). Yield to pressure = céder. Yield returns = rapporter.

m: Enthusiastic or passionate.
Self-evident or unquestionable.
t: Same as « axiome »: no proof needed.

m: To come or bring to an end.
Relating to a person's body; tangible.
Seeking to impose a doctrine without regard to practical considerations.
Departing from literal meaning; metaphorical.
Agitated and confused.
t: A flustered speaker loses the thread: « décontenancé ».

m: Peculiar or individual to one person.
t: Same as « idiosyncrasie »: your own mix.

m: Happening as a minor accompaniment; secondary.
t: Related to « incident ». Incidental expenses = frais accessoires.

m: A consequence of an action; a branching out.
t: Same as « ramification »: ramus = branch. Ramifications are consequences that branch out.

m: To go beyond the range or limits of.
A formal written work dealing systematically with a subject.
In a careful or cautious manner, to avoid harm or damage.
e: Probably Old French gensor (more delicate), from gent (graceful, well-born). Nothing to do with ginger.
t: Not from « gingembre ». Think « gentil »: handle it gently. Lift the lid gingerly.

m: Expressing feelings, especially gratitude or praise, in a gushing, unrestrained way.
t: Same family as « effusion » (« effusions de joie »): feelings pour out. Effusive praise.
